body_markdown:
In 2028, a Ford factory team will once again compete in the World Rally Championship and will inspire a new generation of road cars along the way.


Ford’s history in rallying goes back more than 50 years and created icons out of the Escort,[RS200](https://www.hagerty.com/media/lists/10-hero-cars-of-group-b-rallying/) , Sierra, and Focus as they claimed three manufacturers’ titles for the factory and countless rally wins for drivers such as Hannu Mikkola, Björn Waldegård, Ari Vatanen, Carlos Sainz, Juha Kankkunen, and Colin McRae, to name but a few.

Ford Racing


The U.K.’s[M-Sport,](https://www.m-sport.co.uk/) which has run Ford rally cars for the last 30 years, will remain a key partner in developing and operating the WRC Rally1 cars under new regulations which will come online in 2027. The rules, which are aimed at keeping costs down and the excitement levels up, will see cars built around a tubular frame safety cell, with constructors given the freedom to create whatever bodywork they like, rather than requiring WRC cars to mimic production models. Power will come from a 1.6-liter, 290-hp, turbocharged engine running on sustainable fuel, driving all four wheels via a five-speed transmission. Suspension design and overall dimensions are also determined in the rules. Crucially, there’s a cost cap of €345,000 ($390,000), which is less than half of the price of 2026’s cars, making the sport more appealing to Ford.


M-Sport currently fields the Ford Puma in the top tier of the World Rally Championship, and will get Ford’s full backing for the 2028 season, before debuting an all-new vehicle in 2029—most likely based on the next Ford Fiesta hatchback. Ford recently announced its plan for Europe, focused on building cars for its “perfectly imperfect roads,” and a rally-ready Fiesta would be just that.


“You can’t fake it on Europe’s roads, which is why a car’s responsiveness and handling matters,” says Jim Baumbick, President, Ford Europe. “The WRC is the ultimate proving ground for control and driver engagement, and that is the exact spirit and lessons learned we are injecting into our next generation of passenger vehicles.”


“Rallying is where Ford’s character faces its toughest test, and where generations of fans come to share the thrill of seeing a car take on the impossible. We want our next generation of European vehicles to carry that same unapologetic spirit. Responsive, confidence-inspiring, and rewarding to drive on the roads people use every day.”
